text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
- The high pace of credit growth going to firms and individuals has been continuing for several months. Ever higher real interest rates continue as do central bank warnings of an impending crisis.
- The Supreme Administrative Court has accepted the placing of the A-4 toll motorway from the Opole province to the town of Gliwice in southern Poland.
Trader Universal has not bid for shares in the Romet bicycle maker as previously planned. Unofficial sources say the U.S.'s Poland Growth Fund, a co-owner of Bank Komunalny, bid.
The first food-price rises stemming from recent flooding are taking place, largely hitting sugar, which was up 10 percent on southern Poland's Malopolska commodities exchange.
- Analysts say the current flooding in Poland will not cause heavy price rises though such estimates are made with no firm data on flood damage.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
